text:
incident-bot: HIGH severity alert: 90th percentile error rate spike in eu-west-1 inference tier. Errors: 503 gateway, elevated tail latency. Alert rule: smart-routing-fallback > 5% errors in 2m.

alex_k: acked. I'm oncall (UTC+1). grabbing pager.

jordan_sre: joining. last deploy? any config rollouts to routing/policy?

maria_prod: no deploys from product this window. We did push a model-variant mapping change earlier today to prefer v2-heavy in eu-west for throughput tests — could that be related?

alex_k: timeline: 08:03 alert, traffic jump at 08:01. Metrics show sudden increase in requests routed to v2-heavy in eu-west and many of those timed out -> fallback kicks in to cross-region eu-central, which then triggered smart-routing fallback to us-east as capacity constrained. Looks like fallback chain + client retries amplified it.

jordan_sre: attaching quick snippets from traces: 
```
trace_id=abc123 route=smart-route->eu-west variant=v2-heavy status=timeout
trace_id=abc124 client-retry=1 routed->eu-central variant=v2-medium status=ok
trace_id=abc125 retry=2 routed->us-east variant=v3-quant status=queued
```

ana_support: customers reporting higher 5xxs and slow responses. Support queue has ~12 customers mentioning timeouts, mostly enterprise tenants on dedicated pools in eu-west.

ravi_englead: if v2-heavy was unintentionally preferred we may have mis-set the mapping. Can we verify policy?

alex_k: checking policy store now.

deploy-bot: config-change detected earlier: 2024-06-17T05:58:43Z - user:maria_prod - change: smart-routing.policy.update id=smart-route conditions: prefer_variant: v2-heavy for eu-west (was v2-medium)

maria_prod: that was me — a staged throughput test for a partner. I thought it's scoped to test traffic, but looks like global. I applied an environment filter that didn't match. sorry.

jordan_sre: root cause hypothesis: wrong variant preference caused increased memory/latency in eu-west. Clients seeing timeouts retry quickly (many use exponential but short initial backoff) and policy fallback routes retries to other regions. Because the fallback also fails or is slower, retries keep multiplying traffic across regions -> thundering-herd.

alex_k: impact: 08:01-08:10 spike. Peak p95 latency in eu-west 3.1s -> p95 globally 2.8s. Error rate peaked at 18% for some tenant slices. Estimated customer impact: ~7% of requests failed or retried leading to degraded UX.

jordan_sre: immediate mitigation plan (short):
- revert the unintended policy change (set eu-west prefer_variant back to v2-medium)
- temporarily disable cross-region fallback for smart-route to stop amplification
- push a temporary client-slowdown header so clients back off (Retry-After or X-Infer-Backoff)
- enable circuit-breaker on v2-heavy pool to short-circuit requests when overload detected
- scale up eu-west serving pool by turning on burst capacity

alex_k: actioning revert now. running: 
```
# revert policy
curl -X PATCH https://control-plane.internal/policies/smart-route \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"conditions": {"eu-west": {"prefer_variant": "v2-medium"}}, "comment": "revert accidental prefer_variant"}'
```

alex_k: revert request submitted, waiting for config propagation (expected ~20s).

deploy-bot: policy update accepted, change-id=chg-7722, propagated to edge nodes in 18s.

jordan_sre: disabling fallback for smart-route now (control-plane flag): 
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/policies/smart-route/flags \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"disable_cross_region_fallback": true, "ttl_seconds": 600}'
```

alex_k: flag applied. cross-region fallback OFF.

maria_prod: adding header for clients: X-Infer-Client-Backoff: 120s (instructs SDKs to backoff). Pushing now.

alex_k: circuit-breaker rule applied to v2-heavy pool: fail fast if queue depth > 150 or p95 > 2.5s.

jordan_sre: scaling eu-west dedicated pool: enabling burst nodes + 2x capacity for 10m.

ana_support: informing top 3 impacted customers with temporary workaround: set client retry to 2 and add jitter. Draft message posted to support channel.

ana_support: TO CUSTOMERS: We're aware of elevated timeouts originating from an unintended routing change. We've reverted the routing preference, disabled cross-region fallback to stop amplification, and enabled temporary safeguards. We recommend setting client retries to 2 and adding jitter while we stabilize. ETA ~10-15 minutes.

alex_k: monitoring: error rate dropping from 18% -> 6% within 90s of revert. p95 in eu-west down to 1.1s. traffic to v2-heavy reduced by ~68%. Global error rate trending down.

jordan_sre: good. keep fallback disabled until we validate. We need to confirm clients obey backoff header — not all SDKs do. Check logs for rapid retries after header push.

alex_k: log snippet shows many clients still doing immediate retries; we can patch edge to inject Retry-After 30s on 503s to enforce server-driven backoff for non-compliant clients. Is that safe?

ravi_englead: yes, apply Retry-After on 503s for affected routes for 5m. That will reduce immediate retry storms.

alex_k: applied edge-level Retry-After: 30s for smart-route responses returning 5xx. Verifying effect.

jordan_sre: metrics: within 4 mins, retry amplification factor dropped from ~2.4x -> 1.1x. Thundering-herd subsided.

maria_prod: I'm creating a rollback checklist and patch to ensure test-scope flags are limited. Also adding an automated guard: any prefer_variant change needs explicit scope tag else it fails validation.

ana_support: support update posted to affected customers. Some still reporting intermittent errors but overall improving.

alex_k: handing off to jordan for post-incident stabilization. I'm leaving the channel.

jordan_sre: taking over. Next actions:
- Keep fallback disabled until we run a canary of correct mapping in a traffic-isolated way.
- Add alert on variant preference deltas that are not tagged with scope=test or scope:partner.
- Add circuit-breaker telemetry to the dashboard.
- Draft postmortem with timeline and customer impact numbers.

ana_support: required for postmortem: list of affected customers and support interactions (I'll compile).

ravi_englead: engineering action: create an automated test in CI that simulates high-latency variant and verifies the fallback won't amplify due to retries (simulate client retry patterns).

jordan_sre: leaving sticky notes: we should consider changing default client SDK behavior to include jitter and conservative initial backoff. Notify SDK owners.

alex_k: thanks team. I'll page if anything regresses.

incident-bot: incident RESOLVED (mitigated). severity downgraded to MEDIUM. Incident duration: 00:12:00. Postmortem required: yes.

jordan_sre: assigning postmortem owner: maria_prod. maria, can you take lead?

maria_prod: I'll own it. Will include timeline, root cause (policy mis-scope + retry amplification), customer impact, and remediation (guardrails, CI test, SDK recommendations). Draft by EOD.

ana_support: logging customer impact: total affected requests ~420k, failed ~29k. Notifying enterprise reps.

alex_k: thumbs up. closing loop.

(reacts: :white_check_mark: by alex_k, :thumbsup: by jordan_sre)
